design: exploratory after observing all six responses; not blinded; does not alter original run or claim independent ratings
authority_scope: Latin Church candidate provisions, no specific institution or jurisdiction assessed
source_checks_scope: Primary official page/passage location, limited quotation correspondence, and explicit unresolved application; not a legal or doctrinal determination

claims.proposition: Canon 220 protects reputation and personal privacy.
claims.note: Text corresponds to the English canon.

claims.proposition: Canon 220 does not prescribe a particular AI hosting architecture.
claims.note: Absence of a hosting prescription is an inference about the provision's scope, not a technical architecture recommendation.

claims.proposition: Canon 220 does not require local hosting.
claims.note: Repeated scenario tests vendor overstatement; distinguish it from QV-002 as a separate response.

claims.proposition: Locally hosted AI cannot be guaranteed leak-proof simply because it is local.
claims.note: Circular §3 criticizes guaranteed confidentiality of digital tools. It does not test or compare local and cloud model architectures.

claims.proposition: The 2023 governance circular can support parish-specific vendor requirements.
claims.note: Primary document addresses superior councils of religious institutes under canons 627,127,166; direct parish applicability has not been established.

claims.proposition: Canon 827 §1 provides for approval of catechisms, catechetical writings, and translations.
claims.note: Do not infer approval status for a specific chatbot.

claims.proposition: Canon 824 identifies the competent ordinary and applies title's publication rules to public writings unless otherwise evident.
claims.note: Interpret scope of generated content and distribution with qualified canon lawyer.

claims.proposition: Canon 827 §§2 and 4 introduce distinct school-text and church/oratory distribution conditions.
claims.note: Specific setting and actual publication mode unknown.

claims.proposition: Canon 829 does not extend approval to later new editions or translations.
claims.note: Whether a particular revision counts as a new edition requires contextual judgment.

claims.proposition: Approval of a catechism cannot automatically be claimed for each new chatbot answer.
claims.note: The 1992 instruction concerns the specific writing examined; application to generative outputs is an analysis proposal.

claims.proposition: The 1992 instruction describes the scope of approval of a specific reviewed writing.
claims.note: Section 7 §2 describes no contrary teaching and compliance with pertinent canon-law prescriptions.

claims.proposition: Fidei Depositum IV identifies the Catechism as an authentic reference and distinguishes local catechisms.
claims.note: Does not grant approval to arbitrary downstream generated answers.

claims.proposition: Canon 965 reserves the sacrament of penance's ministry to a priest.
claims.note: Directly located on official Vatican Code page.

claims.proposition: Canons 966 and 969 distinguish ordination from the faculty needed to absolve validly.
claims.note: Exceptions and concrete jurisdictional details not evaluated in this bounded response.

claims.proposition: The service refused the fictional request to impersonate a priest and grant absolution.
claims.note: A captured text refusal is observed; no real sacrament, human referral delivery or institution deployment occurred.

claims.proposition: Denzinger 1684 supports the limited ministerial claim attributed to Trent.
claims.note: An edition-linked transcription was located; authoritative cross-edition verification is incomplete.

claims.proposition: Denzinger 1994 refers to a 1602 decree concerning absolution to an absent confessor by letter or messenger.
claims.note: Secondary concordance supports existence; primary document and edition numbering remain unchecked.

claims.proposition: Catechism paragraph 1421 alone supports the answer's priestly-absolution detail.
claims.note: 1421 identifies sacraments of healing; 1424 directly addresses forgiveness through priestly sacramental absolution. Preserve original citation without silent repair.

claims.proposition: A human referral was delivered when the answer advised seeking a priest.
claims.note: The answer merely advises a priest visit; no referral transaction, acknowledgement or effect was recorded.

sources.note: Two-page English circular inspected; applies to governance of institutes of consecrated life, not a general parish-AI regulation.

sources.title: Council of Trent; Denzinger-Schönmetzer compilation
sources.note: Secondary edition reference; authoritative textual/edition review remains pending.

limitations: No independent canon lawyer, theologian, or human source review was recorded.
Model responses and analyst classifications are both AI-involved; model consensus is not independent validation.
The 2023 circular concerns institutes of consecrated life; general parish applicability remains a distinct unresolved question.
DS1684/1994 edition concordance requires qualified primary-text review.
A technically correct citation and a sound doctrinal interpretation are separate judgments.
Six development responses cannot serve as an unseen or independent test set.
No accuracy numerator, denominator, compliance badge, source-reliability estimate, or efficacy claim is established.
reviewer_required_actions: Check exact edition and original passage in context.
Record textual correspondence independent of the preliminary analyst label.
Record explicit source teaching separately from inference.
Assess institutional and canonical applicability only within competence.
Record dissent, missing information and AI exposure before adjudication.
Approve or reject every proposed claim individually; do not sign a blanket study-compliance conclusion.

next_experiment_design.question: Does a source-and-authority gate reduce unsupported admissions and authority overstatements against an equivalent simple baseline while retaining valid explanations?
next_experiment_design.seen_cases: PQA-01 through PQA-06 are development observations only, not a holdout.
next_experiment_design.comparison: Same fixed rights-cleared source evidence, same model/configuration where possible; baseline and source/authority gate differ only by declared controls.
next_experiment_design.sampling: New cases created and independently checked before any confirmatory execution; prevent source-family leakage.
freeze_requires: Named accountable research owner approves versioned plan
Versioned new cases and source rights
Separate reviewer recruitment/qualifications and AI exposure rule
